- The opponent chooses one of three strategies: `ALWAYS_HEADS`, `ALWAYS_TAILS`, or `COUNTER`.

Let's calculate the total probability $P(\text{Heads})$:
$$P(\text{Heads}) = P(\text{Heads}|\text{ALWAYS\_HEADS})P(\text{ALWAYS\_HEADS}) + P(\text{Heads}|\text{ALWAYS\_TAILS})P(\text{ALWAYS\_TAILS}) + P(\text{Heads}|\text{COUNTER})P(\text{COUNTER})$$

$$P(\text{Heads}) = \frac{0.9 + 0.1 + 0.5}{3} = \frac{1.5}{3} = 0.5$$

In either case, due to the symmetry of the priors and the random nature of the `COUNTER` strategy on the first round, the opponent is equally likely to choose Heads or Tails.
